clue.text: Some broad-minded ass ?

parts.note: read literally, broad-minded describes someone whose head is wide or plump, and a dull-witted fool is called by that very phrase

explanation.surface: A tolerant, liberal person who is nonetheless rather foolish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broad-minded' normally means tolerant; here it is taken literally as having a broad (fat) head, which is a slang word for a stupid person.
explanation.definitionFit: A dim-witted person or idiot is commonly insulted as having a thick, plump skull.

clue.text: Happen to quarrel?

explanation.surface: Does it come about that two people argue?
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to come about, occur, and to have a row and stop being friends.

clue.text: Term for old coin round the border

indicators.note: round means the coin goes around the border

parts.note: a tester was an old English sixpence or shilling coin
a rim is an edge or border

explanation.surface: A word for an antique coin with a rim around it.
explanation.walkthrough: A tester (or teston) was an old English coin, a shilling then sixpence of Tudor times.
explanation.definitionFit: A trimester is an academic or pregnancy term of about three months.

clue.text: Leave for quarter to ten tea-break

parts.note: E (east) is one of the four quarters of the compass
X is the Roman numeral ten

indicators.note: break means the letters of tea are broken up and reformed

explanation.surface: Time off from fifteen minutes to ten for a tea break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quarter to ten' looks like 9.45 but gives E before X; 'break' rearranges TEA into EAT. An exeat is permission to be absent, as from a British boarding school or college.
explanation.definitionFit: An exeat is formal permission for absence, as from a school or college.

clue.text: This sort of clue OK? Quite

parts.note: this clue is a down clue
OK means right, correct

explanation.surface: Is this kind of clue acceptable? Entirely.
explanation.definitionFit: Downright as an adverb means thoroughly, utterly.

clue.text: Revelry-used to be connected with sea-trip

parts.note: past tense of be: was
a voyage on the sea is a sail

explanation.surface: Merrymaking that is tied up with a voyage at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Wassail is old-fashioned festive drinking and merrymaking, especially at Christmas.

clue.text: Present-time musicians ?

parts.note: present-time is Christmas, when presents are given, and these are the street singers of that season

explanation.surface: Contemporary musicians, playing now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present-time' looks like 'modern' but means the season of presents. The waits were bands of carol singers and players who went from house to house at Christmas in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Waits were groups of singers or players performing carols door to door at Christmas.

clue.text: Bird, she's superior to many a male one

indicators.note: in a down clue superior to means placed above, so first

parts.note: taken as written, the word she
L is the Roman numeral 50, many
a drake is a male duck, a male bird

explanation.surface: A female bird ranks above many males of her kind.
explanation.definitionFit: The shelduck's male is called a sheldrake, a large colourful duck.

clue.text: His income is derived from principal

definitions.text: His income is derived from principal

parts.words: His income is derived from principal
parts.note: principal reads as capital money but means the person he acts for, who pays him commission

explanation.surface: An investor living off his capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Principal' suggests a capital sum earning interest; it means the client for whom a representative acts.
explanation.definitionFit: A representative acting on someone's behalf is paid by the person he represents, his principal.

clue.text: Robber led Nora astray

indicators.note: going astray means wandering off course, so the letters stray into a new order

explanation.surface: A thief lured Nora off the right path.
explanation.definitionFit: A ladrone is an archaic word for a robber or bandit, from Spanish ladrón.

clue.text: Oil spilled about the river

indicators.note: oil that is spilled is scattered about, so its three letters are jumbled

parts.note: re is Latin-derived 'concerning', i.e. about

explanation.surface: Oil leaked around a river, a pollution incident.
explanation.definitionFit: The Loire is the longest river in France.

clue.text: British philosopher shows sign of age ?

explanation.surface: A British thinker displays evidence of growing old.
explanation.walkthrough: Alfred North Whitehead was a British philosopher and mathematician; a head of white hair is a sign of age.
explanation.definitionFit: A. N. Whitehead was an English philosopher; white hair on the head marks advancing years.

clue.text: Upsets public, N.U.R.'s outing.

parts.note: overt means open, done in public

indicators.note: an outing is a trip away, here sending these letters off into a new order

parts.note: NUR was the National Union of Railwaymen; with its S these give four letters

explanation.surface: A railway union's day trip upsets the public.
explanation.walkthrough: The NUR was Britain's National Union of Railwaymen; its letters plus the S of the possessive are rearranged ('outing') into URNS.
explanation.definitionFit: To overturn something is to upset it, literally or by reversing a decision.

clue.text: Abroad, said to be the same

definitions.text: Abroad, said to be the same

parts.words: Abroad, said to be the same
parts.note: in Italy (abroad) the word for 'said' was borrowed into English to mean 'as already said', i.e. the same again

explanation.surface: Overseas, people are reported to be just alike.
explanation.walkthrough: The English word comes from Italian detto, 'said', used for 'the aforesaid'; so the foreign word for 'said' stands for 'the same'.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is used to mark repetition of what is written above, meaning likewise or identical.

clue.text: In 'Tibet, it used to identify the emperor

indicators.note: in signals the letters lie inside the words Tibet, it used

explanation.surface: In Tibet, a certain sign was once used to mark out the emperor.
explanation.definitionFit: Titus was a Roman emperor, son of Vespasian.

clue.text: Someone looking in weekly ?

explanation.surface: A person watching inside each week.
explanation.walkthrough: The Spectator is a British weekly magazine of politics and culture.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectator is an onlooker or viewer; The Spectator is a London weekly magazine.

clue.text: Wiseacre resorted to the Magi

indicators.note: resorted read as re-sorted, sorted again into a new order

explanation.surface: A know-all went off to consult the three wise men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resorted' looks like 'went to' but is read as re-sorted. The Wise Men of Gotham were villagers of English folklore famous for foolish deeds, so a Gothamite is an ironic wise man.
explanation.definitionFit: A man of Gotham is proverbially a foolish would-be sage, like a wiseacre who thinks himself clever.

clue.text: Man in train smash is an old sailor

indicators.note: in places the man inside the smashed train
a smash breaks something to pieces, so the letters are reassembled

parts.note: Paul is a man's name

explanation.surface: A man caught up in a train crash turns out to be an elderly seaman.
explanation.definitionFit: Like tar, a tarpaulin was old slang for a seaman, from their tarred canvas hats.

clue.text: Rude about a number appearing unable to pay

indicators.note: about means the rude word goes around the number

parts.note: insolent means rude, disrespectful
V is the Roman numeral five

explanation.surface: Someone rude about a figure is revealed as broke.
explanation.definitionFit: Insolvent means bankrupt, lacking money to meet debts.

clue.text: Worker is a transport man a writer at heart

indicators.note: at heart puts the writer in the middle of the transport man

parts.note: a carter carts goods by horse and wagon
a pen is a writing implement

explanation.surface: A labourer is a haulier who is at heart an author.
explanation.definitionFit: A carpenter is a skilled tradesman who works wood.

clue.text: Roman general appears stupid to us

parts.note: crass means grossly stupid

explanation.surface: A Roman commander seems foolish to us.
explanation.definitionFit: Marcus Licinius Crassus was a Roman general and triumvir with Caesar and Pompey.

clue.text: She takes one in otherwise

indicators.note: takes ... in means the word for otherwise swallows the numeral

parts.note: else means otherwise
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: She accepts someone in a different way.
explanation.definitionFit: Elsie is a girl's name, so it can stand for any woman, a she.

clue.text: Properties in 'N. and S. Carolina?

parts.note: the Carolinas are each a state, so lands lying in such states are the properties described

explanation.surface: Real estate listings in the two Carolinas.
explanation.walkthrough: North and South Carolina are both US states; the clue plays on property, real holdings, sitting in states.
explanation.definitionFit: Landed properties are estates, and the Carolinas themselves are states.

clue.text: Like to put item in balance sheet?

parts.note: as means like, in the manner of
to set something is to put it down

explanation.surface: An accountant wants to enter something on the balance sheet.
explanation.definitionFit: Assets are the things of value listed on one side of a balance sheet.

clue.text: Shut up dwarf in cupboard, perhaps

parts.note: sh is the call for silence, shut up
an elf is a small sprite, like a dwarf

explanation.surface: Lock a dwarf in a cupboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shut up' looks like 'lock away' but is SH, hush.
explanation.definitionFit: A shelf is a horizontal board, such as is found inside a cupboard.

clue.text: Farm in built-up belt-twig ?

indicators.note: in places the farm word within the jumbled belt
built up suggests the letters of belt are reconstructed into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: a ranch is a large farm

explanation.surface: A farm inside the built-up green belt, with a twig.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Built-up' is an anagram signal: BELT becomes BLET, and RANCH goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A branchlet is a small branch, a shoot or twig.

clue.text: Philosopher smoked ?

explanation.surface: A thinker who has been puffing on a pipe.
explanation.walkthrough: Francis Bacon was an English philosopher; bacon is often smoked cured pork.
explanation.definitionFit: Francis Bacon was an English thinker; cured pork is commonly sold smoked or unsmoked.

clue.text: Ring of metal

parts.note: ring reads as a circlet but means the loud resonant sound struck metal makes

explanation.surface: A metal band.
explanation.definitionFit: A clang is a loud resonant noise, like that of struck iron.

clue.text: Two hundred pies at roughly a pound ? Doubtful

indicators.note: roughly suggests a rough, inexact rendering, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral 100, so two of them make two hundred
L, from Latin libra, is the abbreviation for a pound

explanation.surface: Two hundred pies at about a pound each? A dubious deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roughly' shuffles CC with PIESAT into SCEPTICA; L for pound, from libra, follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sceptical means being inclined to doubt or question.

clue.text: Thoroughly proficient in a part of the business

parts.note: dept, short for department, is a section of a firm

explanation.surface: Fully skilled in one department of the company.
explanation.definitionFit: An adept is highly skilled, an expert.

clue.text: Colour associated in Essex with Thoreau's work

definitions.text: Colour associated in Essex with Thoreau's work

parts.words: Colour associated in Essex with Thoreau's work
parts.note: Thoreau's book is Walden; the Essex town of that name is prefixed by a yellow-orange colour

explanation.surface: A colour linked, in an English county, with an American writer's book.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry David Thoreau wrote Walden; Saffron Walden is a market town in Essex, an English county, named for the crocus once grown there.
explanation.definitionFit: Saffron is a deep orange-yellow colour, from the spice of crocus stigmas.

clue.text: Nullifies 7 unusual directions

indicators.note: unusual means the letters are put in an out-of-the-ordinary order

parts.note: refers to the answer to 7 down, a representative acting for a principal
E and S are compass directions, east and south

explanation.surface: Cancels out seven odd instructions.
explanation.walkthrough: '7' points to the solution of 7 down; 'unusual' rearranges it, and the compass points E and S follow.
explanation.definitionFit: To negate something is to cancel or invalidate it.
